**Finding: compliant (preferred position).**

The Kubient MSA imposes no exclusivity on AP. Section 1 affirmatively negates it: "Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties."

I checked every other place exclusivity could hide:
- **Scope/licence (§§1–3, p0002–p0014):** the licence to us is expressly non-exclusive; "Inventory," "Auction," and "Services" contain no requirements or minimum-volume commitment, no first-look and no right of first refusal.
- **Other "exclusive" hits:** New York merits forum (p0064), each Party's own marks (p0065), entire-agreement language (p0072), third-party beneficiaries (p0073) — none bind our sourcing freedom.
- **§5 Fees (p0023):** Kubient is "responsible for contracting with all advertisers... on Customer's behalf, including Advertisers with whom Customer has existing relationships," unless an Exhibit provides otherwise. Noted in the rationale rather than flagged: it allocates Kubient's delivery role and is expressly subject to our §1 freedom to sell through other agents, so it is not exclusive dealing. If any Exhibit later adds a channel-restriction, that Exhibit should be reviewed against this rule.

No redline proposed, since the clause already sits at the preferred position rather than the fallback.
